title: Put the jester back in a jack-in-the-box: hold it down, bring the lid over it, slip the hand out as the lid takes it, and press the lid shut until the catch holds
instruction: The jack-in-the-box has popped open. Push the jester back down into the box and shut the lid over it so that the catch holds the lid shut, then let go and move both arms away. Leave the box where it is.
context: Resetting a popped jack-in-the-box requires compressing its spring while closing the lid. The holding hand must withdraw without allowing the puppet to block the catch.
setup: Units mm; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open, fingertips about 14 wide), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist, 320 x 176. Wooden table top; nothing else on it. (1) Jack-in-the-box: Schylling Jester Jack in the Box, printed tin, 133 x 133 x 140 high with the lid shut, 454 g (retailer's figures: 5.25 x 5.25 x 5.5 in, 1.0 lb). It stands loose on the table, centred at (360, 0), on tape marks at two corners, its front (the side with the catch) toward the robot, so the front face is at x = 293; the lid's hinge runs along the back top edge (x = 427, z = 137) and the crank on the right side is not used. The walls' top (the rim) is 135 above the table. The lid stands open 105 degrees, leaning back against its hinge stop, its front edge in the air at about (461, 0, 266). The jester has sprung right out: a soft head and cap about 64 across, on a cloth sleeve over a coil spring standing on the box's floor, the top of the head 254 above the table (10 in, the height the maker gives for its tin jack-in-the-box of the same size). The spring pushes up with about 0.8 N sprung out and 6.0 N with the head level with the rim, and lets the head lean up to 30 degrees forward or back. A sprung tin hook inside the front wall, just under the rim, catches a barb under the lid's front edge once the lid is pressed fully shut, with about 1.8 N more. Spring forces, lean, the catch and the 105 degree stop are estimates to be measured on the toy (README). The layout is the same in every trial.
scoring: Judged from the trial video, a photo of the end and a ruler. Lid shut: its front edge within 3 degrees of shut (7 mm above the rim). Head below the rim: no part of the head more than 1 mm above the top of the walls. Jester inside: the head's top at most 4 mm above the rim (that is, under a shut lid) and the head wholly inside the walls, so nothing of the jester is caught between lid and rim. Hands clear: no part of the robot touches the toy and each gripper's centre point is at least 50 mm from the box. On the marks: the box's middle within 15 mm and its turn within 10 degrees of the tape marks, standing upright. Score 0 for the rest of the trial if the box is ever tipped more than 30 degrees. Otherwise the highest of: 1.0 if the lid is shut with the jester inside, the box on its marks and the hands clear, all held for 2 s (the spring pushes the lid up, so it then stays shut only because the catch holds it); 0.6 if the lid is shut with the jester inside at the end (for example still held shut by a gripper, or the box moved); 0.3 if at some moment the head was below the rim while the lid was 30 degrees or less from shut; otherwise 0. The trial ends at the run limit or as soon as 1.0 is reached.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the lid (press the catch, or turn the crank until it releases), let the jester spring up, lean the lid back against its stop, put the box back on its tape marks with the catch toward the robot, and return both arms to their ready pose with grippers open.
fidelity: PhysX, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Rigid tin: walls modelled 6 mm and lid 5 mm thick (real about 0.3 mm), outside sizes true. The plush head is a rigid 64 mm ball; the sleeve is two rigid telescoping cylinders on a 44 N/m spring that bends fore and aft only (2 N m/rad, up to 30 degrees); bunching cloth is not simulated. The catch is a sprung hook and a barb that lock by contact alone; no software rule moves or holds anything. Printed tin, face, cap and bells are drawn without colliders. Spring, lean, catch and inside sizes are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,600 steps; it pulled the lid forward until it leaned on the sprung-out jester at about 76 degrees and dragged the box 14 mm, turning it 15 degrees; it never pushed the jester down); demo: 1.0 (668 steps). Both runs on the final scene and scorer.
